0.d:
This Generative Token is the first GT minted on fxhash.

It also servers as the actual logo of the platform. It represents the generative processes driving fxhash tokens. Generative Tokens are fed with a unique hash to produce unique outputs based on the hash — they are functions with a hash as single input.

The growth that comes out of the text is driven by a "Dividing-Aggregating Walkers" (DAW) algorithm. The hash drives all the DAW settings, as well as a mutation factor which is responsible for changes in each Walker parameters as they divide.

Some iterations will produce very simple outputs whereas others might be more chaotic.

Piece by @ciphrd for fxhash

65.d:
Musical counterpoint is to me an abstraction of the layered, intertwining rhythms of every activity we carry on in our lives. With a global tempo typically set in days, we fit all sorts of temporal structures where our joys and fears live and play out over the span of our lives. This series is a metaphorical transposition of the musical counterpoint into a visual space, sometimes with repeating patterns, sometimes with broken structures, sometimes isolated notes / hours / souls.

Artwork by Marcelo Soria-Rodríguez, @msoriaro. Made with p5js & glsl.

25% of the proceedings in the primary sale once the project is sold out will go to Project Lighthouse, an initiative by Sultan Akif to foster self-sustainable communities in impoverished regions of the world by empowering the youth with access to education and career-long mentoring. See https://libraryinaweek.com/collections/project-lighthouse for more info.

86.d:
The formal structure of a book is beautiful by itself, but its aesthetic is the tacit atmosphere within which events take place in a story.

The WebGL real-time animation sets up an initial grid based on the fxhash. The grid cells get subdivided into another grid and the resulting cells become filled with pixels in color (~33%) or black and white (~66%).
The colored pixels come in 3 different coloring styles.
- Big Palette (~49%)
- Small Palette (~49%)
- Monochrome [b/w] (~2%)
4 noise algorithms modify the pixels of selected grid cells while at the same time 4 reset algorithms reassemble the initial image. The selected cells switch over time.

90.d:
REFLECTOR is an exploration of reflecting rays of light in two-dimensions by Juhani Halkomäki.

The pieces consist of 100 to 1200 rays of light that bounce two times when colliding with an object or the edge of the canvas. Some may seem more beautiful than others but they all have the same internals.

---
Features info
---

Dark mode - Paint the background black
Monochrome - No colors just grays
Emitter mode - One of the following: EDGE, SHAPE, POINT, GRID

Number Of Shapes - How many shapes are on the scene (1-4)
Number of Rays - How many rays are emitted (100-1000)
Number of Bounces - How many times the rays bounce (2-3)
Ray spreading - How much the ray angles are spread (10-100)

Color mode - Either SMOOTH or STEPS
Color spectrum size - How wide hue spectrum is used
Color spectrum offset - How much the hue is offset
Color step interval - How many consecutive rays should have the same color
Color step count - How many steps is the color spectrum divided into

95.d:
Breakfast is a real-time generative system for creating complex arrangements of primitive forms. Inspired by suprematism, its aim is to arrange simple and boldly coloured shapes in pleasing ways. Driven by a real-time physics engine, it allows for direct collaboration between artist, audience, and generative system. 

Original artwork by Kelly Milligan (kellymilligan.art) in Titirangi, Auckland, New Zealand - Published November 2021 on fxhash.xyz
95.c:
Breakfast is a real-time generative system for creating complex arrangements of primitive forms. Inspired by suprematism, its aim is to arrange simple and boldly coloured shapes in pleasing ways. Driven by a real-time physics engine, it allows for direct collaboration between artist, audience, and generative system. 

Original artwork by Kelly Milligan (kellymilligan.art) in Titirangi, Auckland, New Zealand - Published November 2021 on fxhash.xyz

Upon sale of final token:
- 20% of proceeds will be donated to Forest & Bird (https://www.forestandbird.org.nz/) for conservation efforts within Aotearoa (New Zealand)
- 5% of proceeds will be sent to @liabru (brm.io) for his work on Matter.js

Controls:
- Save: CMD/CTRL + S - Save as a 4096x4096 still image
- Churn*: C or OPTION/ALT + C to toggle churning and direction
- Gravity*: G to toggle gravity
- Bounce*: B to toggle bounciness
* Exclusive to tokens containing the feature

Notes: 
- Churners move for 15s each minute as an abstract clock, disabled by controls

111.d:
MOYO is generative piece building unique patterns.
The first algorithm was created in 2018, while visiting Kanazawa, a city on the west side of Japan.
Originally inspired by some kimono embroidery, I created some set of rules that will give life, recursively, to patterns generated inside a squared area.

Thanks to fxhash, I can pursue the original generative vision of those patterns by evolving the algorithm, and here comes MOYO.
This collection of 1024 pieces waiting to be minted offers new compositions, new rules and new colors.
During the iterative crafting process, I've been surprised by the algorithm which offered some unexpected kind of results, which have been kept for the final generation.

Artist: Florian Zumbrunn
@florianzumbrunn

147.d:
A Pico-8 demake of my Entropy series previously made on the TIC-80. Due to many of the limitations baked into the Pico-8, this version lacks many of the features from the TIC-80 version, as well having a lower speed, and lower resolution. However, it also has some new features, like mirroring, that provide an interesting twist. fxhash Features are enabled in order to track rarity, there are some rare features like mirror type, or brush_wiggle (which decreases the stability of the visual equilibrium).

This piece is build on the `aebrer_engine` codebase I have developed for Pico-8.

creator: Andrew E. Brereton
date: 2021-11-15
twitter: @aebrer
website: aebrer.xyz
platform: Pico-8, Lua

185.d:
Immutable Mosaic is a (very) humble tribute to all artists in History who created those amazing tiles, stained glass or mosaics. At every iteration, a unique composition of tiles is created in 3D with custom shapes, materials, colors, thickness. But we aren't constrained by reality so our tiles are living matter with evolving textures and light interactions.

Moreover these scenes are interactive so don't hesitate to navigate and find your best point of view to observe light and texture effects.

Controls:
- Double left-click to stop/start camera move.
- Hold left-click to orbit around object.
- Hold right-click to pan camera.

Best rendering on PC with GPU and full screen to enjoy volumetric effects. It works on mobile despite lower quality & potential lagging.

Immutable Mosaic by @naibdian 2021

221.d:
3.1415926535....

Computing Pi is deeply routed in human history. 

We can get an estimate for pi (π) via randomly placing coins on square containing a circle. The more iterations, the more precise the median (middle) estimate for pi will be.

The greater the precision of pi; the greener the output.

Technicalities and Probabilties (P()):

P(Coin In Circle) ≈ Area Of Circle / Area Of Square = πr^2 / 4r^2
P(Coin In Circle) ≈ π/4

P(Coin in Circle) = extracted from number of coins in the circle vs out, by randomly placing coins:
= (coins in circle/ coins out of circle) 

P(Coin In Circle) ≈ π/4
π ≈ 4 x (coins in circle ÷ coins out of circle)

A grid of trailing shapes. Each shape in the line wants to be like the shape in front of it.

The traits
4 shapes: square, cross, triangle, circle
5 grid sizes 1->5 with 1x1 grids being rarest (5%)
2 fill styles: hollow (80%, crosses can't be hollow) and filled (20%)
20% chance for all shapes to be the same
6 color palettes:
- Coffee and Blueberry
- Tropicana
- Monochrome
- Spectrum
- Peach and Pear
- Goji and Kelp

Made by Sam Tsao (@sam___tsao)
